 Prue Leith says having no friends is ‘one of life’s few regrets’
 At 86 years old, the TV chef has realised that it was ‘unwise’ to neglect her friendships
 Annabel Nugent Monday 16 November 2026 04:11 EST

 Prue Leith has said that her lack of friends is one of the “few regrets of her life”, urging younger women to invest in their friendships. 
 The Great British Bake Off star opened up about her personal life in a recent interview, stating: “I’ve been very bad at friendship. I never thought it was important.” 
 “If someone had said, ‘You don’t have any friends,’ I’d have said, “What do we need friends for?’ It didn’t occur to me it was unwise,” Leith told The Daily Mail . 
 At 86, the TV chef said she has realised where she went wrong, suggesting that perhaps her “very happy” first marriage to South African author and property developer Rayne Kruger was the reason. 
 “When your husband is your best friend you tend to neglect all that,” she said. “He didn’t need friends, and I was perfectly happy with that. I was working in London in the week, coming home on a Thursday, and when I did I was quite happy to have scrambled eggs with the children.” Leith and Kruger shared two children. 
 Her intense work schedule was also a contributing factor, said Leith. “I didn’t want to see anyone else because I was tired from work. Later, I regretted that.” 
 Prue admitted she was lonely when Kruger died, explaining: “I didn’t have friends, didn’t even know my neighbours. It never occurred to me at the time.” 
 Leith and Kruger remained married until 1974, when he died at the age of 80. Their marriage had begun as a secret affair; when they met, Kruger had been married to a close friend of Leith’s mother. 
 open image in gallery Dame Prue Leith is among the highlights at Cheltenham Literature Festival ( (Andrew Matthews/ PA) ) “For 13 years, our relationship was a secret, so it would have restricted all that, but even after it we had more than 25 years of marriage, and we didn’t see the need for friends,” she said. “I never ever went out with just a girlfriend. I didn’t have any. But when he died, I thought, ‘Oops!’
 “Not to even know my neighbours… I’m sure there are lots of people who could have been my friends.” 
 Leith remarried in 2016 to John Playfair, who has helped her branch out in terms of her friendship group. “Unlike me, John is good at friendship. He knows everyone. He has all the friends, and he makes new ones all the time,” she said. Prue Leith says having no friends is ‘one of life’s few regrets’
 This is not the first time that the TV chef has spoken about the importance of building friendships. In her recently published memoir Being Old And Learning to Love It! She urged younger women to put time and effort into that area of their lives. 
 Leith had since found a friend in fellow former Bake Off presenter Sandi Toksvig, who presented the BBC baking competition for two years from 2017 to 2019. 
 open image in gallery Dame Prue Leith is backing a call for primary school children to have cookery lessons in schools (Yui Mok/PA) ( (Yui Mok/PA) ) The pair are at the centre of a travel documentary set in Prue’s native South Africa, which begins on Channel 4 later this month. 
 The documentary follows Leith’s exit from Bake Off in January of this year, ending her nine-series tenure as a judge on the show. Nigella Lawson took her seat alongside Paul Hollywood, Alison Hammond, and Noel Fielding. 
 Leith had decided to step back to work less, spend summers in her garden, and go on holiday in Europe in her later years, explaining that the show’s production schedule had prevented her from doing so. 
 Last month, however, Leith admitted that she felt a “pang” after watching Lawson’s debut on the series. 
 “I didn’t give it up because I didn’t like it. I loved it! And when I watched Nigella Lawson doing her first episode – and by the way, I think she’s terrific at it – I did feel a pang,” she said. “I thought, ‘Why did I leave? That was such a great job.’ But I'm glad I did.”
